apiDocs.title: API Documentation
apiDocs.subtitle: How to integrate your system (or an AI) with this WhatsApp gateway

intro.p1: This is the integration documentation for the gateway's public WhatsApp API. It's written to be read by a developer or pasted directly into an AI's context (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) to generate the integration automatically.
intro.p2: Every message sent is asynchronous: the API responds immediately with a "queued" status, and the final result (delivered, read, failed) arrives via webhook or by querying the status endpoint.

principles.title: Contract principles
principles.idempotency: Idempotency required — every send accepts externalId. Resending the same externalId returns the original message instead of duplicating it. Protects against client retries and double-clicks.
principles.async: Always asynchronous — sending responds with 202 Accepted. The final status arrives via webhook or query.
principles.predictableErrors: Predictable errors — every error has a stable code (string) in addition to the HTTP status. Code against the code, never against the message.
principles.versioned: Versioned in the URL — /v1. Breaking changes create /v2.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.p1: Every authenticated request carries a Bearer token in the header:
auth.p2: Validation compares the SHA-256 of the presented token against the stored hash. The result is cached for 60s.

sendMessage.description: Sends a text message to a WhatsApp number.
sendMessage.toRules: Phone number. Accepts various formats, normalized to E.164 (see normalization section).
sendMessage.externalIdRules: Up to 128 characters. Unique per project. Enables idempotency.
sendMessage.scheduledForRules: ISO 8601, in the future, at most +30 days. If omitted, sends as soon as possible.
sendMessage.preferredAccountRules: UUID of a specific pool account. Tries that account first; if unavailable, falls back to normal selection.
sendMessage.idempotencyNote: 200 OK response: when the externalId already exists, the API returns the original message instead of creating a new one.
sendMessage.errInvalidSchedule: Date in the past or beyond 30 days
sendMessage.errOptedOut: Recipient asked to stop receiving messages (opt-out)
sendMessage.errRateLimit: Exceeded requests-per-minute limit. Respect the Retry-After header
sendMessage.errNoAccounts: No pool account is healthy right now
sendMessage.noAccountsNote: By default the message is accepted and queued even without an available account — it waits until one comes back. The 503 is only returned if the request sends the X-Reject-If-Unavailable: true header, useful for time-sensitive messages (e.g. one-time codes) that don't make sense delivered late.

bulk.description: Sends up to 500 messages in a single request. Each becomes an independent message, distributed across pool accounts.
bulk.partialValidation: partial validation: valid items are accepted, invalid ones are reported individually without aborting the whole batch.

media.description: Sends an image or PDF. The only endpoint with a multipart/form-data contract (the others are JSON) — single recipient only, no bulk version.
media.toRules: Phone number, same normalization as the other endpoints.
media.fileRules: File: image (jpeg/png/webp) or PDF, up to 16MB.
media.externalIdRules: Idempotency, same as the text endpoint.
media.storageNote: The file bytes only travel internally and are never stored beyond what's needed to send it — only the file type and name stay in the message history.

getMessage.description: Checks the current status of a specific message by its messageId.
getMessage.onFailure: On failure, the error field is populated:
getMessage.scopeNote: A project only sees its own messages. Querying another project's messageId returns 404 (not 403), to avoid revealing whether the message exists.

listMessages.description: Lists project messages with filters by status, direction, recipient and period. Supports the parameters: status, direction, to, from, until, limit (max 100) and cursor. Cursor-based pagination:

cancel.description: Cancels a message still in the queue ("queued" status). Returns 409 (MESSAGE_NOT_CANCELABLE) if it's already sending or beyond.

health.description: Returns the overall health of the account pool — doesn't expose phone numbers, the consumer doesn't need to know which ones they are.
health.statusNote: status: healthy (2+ healthy accounts) · degraded (1 account) · unavailable (0 accounts)

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.p1: The gateway makes a POST to the endpoint configured by the project whenever a message's status changes or a reply is received.
webhooks.validationTitle: Required validation on the consumer side:
webhooks.validation1: Recalculate the HMAC over the raw body (before any JSON parsing).
webhooks.validation2: Compare in constant time (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual), never with ===.
webhooks.validation3: Reject timestamps older than 5 minutes — without this, an attacker who captured an old webhook could replay it indefinitely (replay attack).
webhooks.statusEventNote: Fired on: sent, delivered, read, failed.
webhooks.retryNote: Success = HTTP 2xx within 10s. After 6 failures, marked as failed. 4xx (except 429) is not retried — it indicates a configuration error on your endpoint. Respond 2xx immediately and process in the background; processing synchronously before responding causes timeouts and unnecessary retries.

phone.title: Phone normalization
phone.p1: Every number is normalized to E.164 before any operation.
phone.cacheNote: Checking existence on WhatsApp is the final source of truth and runs before sending. The result is cached for 7 days, avoiding repeated lookups — which are themselves a sign of automated behavior.

errors.title: Error code catalog
errors.messageNotFound: Doesn't exist or belongs to another project
errors.missingMediaFile: Media send without an attached file
errors.unsupportedMediaType: File type outside the allowed list

checklist.title: Integration checklist
checklist.item1: Always send externalId to guarantee idempotency in case of a retry on your side.
checklist.item2: Code against the error's code, never against the message (which can change).
checklist.item3: Implement the webhook endpoint and validate the HMAC signature before trusting the body.
checklist.item4: Respond 2xx to the webhook immediately and process in the background.
checklist.item5: Handle RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and DAILY_QUOTA_EXCEEDED by respecting the Retry-After header.
checklist.item6: Don't send to numbers that already opted out — the API already blocks it, but check for RECIPIENT_OPTED_OUT before retrying.
